correctness.rationale: Each unselected edge of the prism has precisely the four neighboring edges used in the three exact local Boolean conditions. The 64-state pair transfer is in bijection with arbitrary cyclic selected-edge sets, for every n>=3. Exact enumeration of all 512 candidate local triples gives 102 arcs; positive-return search on all 64 states leaves only one self-loop and one six-cycle, checked with the standalone package code. This fixed finite reachability lemma is sufficient for all n and proves the full two-term polynomial; independent direct edge-endpoint checks through n=7 corroborate but do not replace that proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A dominating induced matching constrains every edge, including selected edges. The six proper perfect edge dominating sets produced here contain adjacent selected edges and cannot be induced matchings. The earlier no-DIM result is therefore compatible with, and does not imply, the new complete perfect-edge-domination polynomial. Perfect edge domination is also distinct from vertex domination and paired domination of prisms.

value.rationale: The 2026 enumeration literature motivates exact counts of all PED sets and identifies broad counting complexity. The result supplies the full cardinality polynomial and all admissible configurations for a standard infinite cubic graph family, with a sharp modular phase transition: only the complete edge set for 6 nondividing n, exactly six additional smaller sets for every multiple of 6. The constant six-way multiplicity on unbounded orders is a meaningful rigidity phenomenon and also distinguishes perfect edge domination from known DIM nonexistence on these graphs. It is not a routine substitution or a small finite table.
